overall_summary: Exoplanet extremes and first-person immersive hypothetical hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') represent the channel's highest-performing content, generating 800-1,000+ views and 3-4% like engagement rates at 19-21 seconds duration. Conversely, generic psychology micro-facts ('Your Brain...') and duplicate re-uploads consistently underperform below 50 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Survival Hypotheses ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (974 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperform third-person expository titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme cosmic and planetary phenomena as high-stakes personal survival simulations.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,032 views, 36 likes, 21s) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes, 19s) show strong viewer retention and engagement compared to sub-16s videos.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain optimal runtime between 19 and 22 seconds, allowing sufficient time for a sensory hook, escalating stakes, and a surprising punchline.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' received 5-53 views across multiple uploads with zero likes or comments; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' stalled at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out passive psychological factoid shorts unless tied to high-stakes visual micro-dramas.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' were re-uploaded multiple times, dropping from early traction to near-zero momentum.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict single-instance topic coverage and prioritize untouched subject entities.
